title: Word link identifiers are interpolated into XML without escaping or validation
reasoning: displayValue is escaped before insertion, but linkId is a public string parameter and is written directly into an XML attribute. A quote or markup character in linkId can corrupt or inject document XML. The same unchecked string is later searched as a substring, and listLinkIds only recognizes lowercase hex/hyphen ids, so the API accepts ids that it cannot reliably list or refresh exactly.
reproduction: Call insertLinkedValue with a linkId containing a double quote, for example x" w:dirty="true. The generated w:tag attribute is malformed or attacker-controlled instead of a single safe tag value.
recommendation: Constrain linkId to the actual supported id grammar, such as a UUID/lowercase hex-hyphen pattern, at insert/create/refresh boundaries. Alternatively escape it for XML attributes and make refresh match the exact tag attribute rather than an arbitrary substring.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The link tests verify escaping for display values, but they only use a safe UUID constant for linkId and do not cover invalid ids, uppercase ids, or prefix collisions.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add word-links tests that reject link ids containing XML-significant characters and that refresh only an exact link id, not a prefix of another id.
minimumFixScope: packages/core/src/links/word-links.ts validation/matching and corresponding link tests.
